svg.aria-label: Figure 2 | Knowledge utility and generative performance
svg.text: Figure 2 | Knowledge utility and generative performance
Matched knowledge conditions distinguish evidence utility from complete-system performance.
a Fixed-pool decision experiment
Identical eligible molecules and hidden measurements
Select candidates in rounds; reveal selected outcomes
Primary contrast: knowledge on minus knowledge off
b Generative system experiment
Shared starting set, rules and oracle-call budget
Different generators and knowledge interfaces
Primary contrast: full system versus strong baselines
Knowledge off
Chemical context retained
No mined-evidence intervention
Applicable knowledge
Reviewed scope matches task
Same underlying evidence
Inapplicable evidence
Matched topic and packet size
Scope mismatch is explicit
c Apply all three conditions within IH-LM, Claude, GPT and Gemini
d Evaluate learning and transfer
Fixed pool: measured yield and selection efficiency
Generation: train-score AUC versus oracle calls
Separate endpoint: final top-10 held-out score
Within-system paired effects and uncertainty
e Evaluate knowledge use and efficiency
Scope rejection and evidence-to-proposal trace
Validity, uniqueness and structural diversity
Failures, latency, tokens and monetary cost
Seeds repeat runs; tasks/sources define transfer
All three conditions are assessed on both outcome groups below
Interpretation: better optimisation scores do not establish better biological activity or permeability.
Final held-out scores and train-objective AUC are separate endpoints, with task-specific effect margins.
Cross-system contrasts compare complete systems; within-system contrasts isolate the knowledge intervention.
